segments.narration: A massive iron pillar built 1,600 years ago refuses to rust. Standing in outdoor heat and monsoon moisture, raw iron should decay within decades.
Ancient blacksmiths had no modern rustproofing or stainless steel. Yet while other ancient metal crumbled away, this six-ton pillar remained untouched.
Did ancient metallurgists unlock secret technology modern science forgot? For centuries, people believed divine magic or extraterrestrial metal protected it.
Microscopic analysis finally solved the mystery. High phosphorus content left over from ancient smelting methods triggered a rare protective chemical shield.
It formed an airtight layer of iron hydrogen phosphate, blocking corrosion forever. Did those ancient smiths deliberately engineer this armor, or was it a total accident?
